paper.title_en: CFT-Inspired Two-Horizon Thermodynamics as a Diagnostic for the Bi-Hair Organization of NUT Charge
paper.abstract_en: After decades without a fully self-consistent thermodynamic formulation, recent proposals for Lorentzian Taub-NUT spacetime have yielded several inequivalent descriptions, each satisfying its own first law and Smarr relation, leaving unresolved which formulation is physically preferred. In this Letter, we introduce a two-horizon diagnostic whose left- and right-moving thermodynamic temperatures are fixed via the harmonic mean relations before the thermodynamic variables are chosen. For uncharged Taub-NUT spacetime, the left-moving first law closes with the mass and NUT charge, whereas, within the restricted homogeneous class examined here, the right-moving first law requires an additional thermodynamic secondary hair $J_n = mn$. This result supports a bi-hair thermodynamic organization of the NUT parameter through $N = n$ and $J_n = mn$. Furthermore, this two-horizon framework offers a new opportunity toward addressing similar thermodynamic non-uniqueness in other two-horizon NUT-charged systems when the first law and Smarr relation alone do not identify a physically preferred formulation.
